The part of [section 9.4 of the fast-connect design](SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md#94-the-deadlines), the N25Q128 at its datasheet maximum, erases a 64 KiB sector in up to 3 s (tSE) and programs a page in up to 5 ms (tPP).

The harness had first to follow KLJ3: its flash device takes writes only in the flash map's journal, 640 KiB at `0xe40000`, and a save's container is the stage less KLJ3's 10-byte record header. 0 refusals; 7 misses of 996 probe instances (4 of 136 paths) at 8x8/2if and of 945 (4 of 87) at 1x1/1if, round 29's seven, the owed rows at 62.68 to 65.05 ms and 61.95 to 63.59 ms; the arm 0 of 736 and 0 of 280; arm B 0 of 39 and 0 of 25; no work pass over the share (257,719 at 8x8/2if, 166,045 at 1x1/1if).

The built design is the option's, then at the slice ruling's 800 us (950 us at the head, [below](#the-final-passs-restatements)): AECP first, and owed-notice slots of 552 B (`AECP_OWED_BYTES`), each holding the largest legal AECPDU, so every legal command's notice is queued and R4L is AECP's burst taken as R4's is.

With the domain's 64 at 1x1/1if, the edit's stack frame moved 192 B and the largest legal command's record rose then from 91,625 CPU cycles to 98,720 by the 8 KiB direct-mapped data cache alone.
- **The images.** Every image's rom was then the same as round 8's or 8 B smaller, and sram and tiles were unchanged (each image at the head: [section 5](#5-fit)).

- **Where the cycles went.** A committed-PC trace of each record, its lines read from a `-g` build of the same code, split the REMOVE: 4,321 commits, 10,397 cycles of short pipeline stalls, 10,349 of instruction-fetch stalls (143 refills of 64 B, nearly all distinct lines) and 2,784 of data stalls. #904's one-pass check (`1b70cedd`) added 1,643 commits to the record before it: `look`'s copy of each row and the REMOVE pass's copy of each kept row were each a call of `memcpy` of 8 B, about 120 cycles, and the edit cleared 960 B of its table whatever its size.

A mapping is copied a coordinate at a time and a row's words are composed in registers, so no edit calls `memcpy` but for its response's rows; the edit clears only the slots `place` forms and each mapping's link, marks and occurrences at its turn in the table, 64 B and 3 B a mapping at 1x1/1if; a REMOVE looks up only the rows of its port's map from the first equal to a held mapping to one past the last, which its FOUND pass holds, keeping those before in place and moving those after down; and the descriptor and page are echoed a byte at a time.

The cut moved every other record of the run by the layout alone: a variant that also wrote the response's rows from the table was 112 B longer and raised every other record of the group by 300 to 400 cycles.
